claims.text: Multi-element chemical disorder creates intrinsic nanoscale lattice distortions in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Nanoscale lattice distortions enhance local magnetoelastic coupling.
Enhanced local magnetoelastic coupling governs a strong magnetocaloric response at applied fields below 1 T.
The proposed distortion-mediated behavior permits rapid heat exchange.
The proposed distortion-mediated behavior maintains low magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed distortion-mediated behavior maintains mechanical stability.
The as-cast alloy has a uniform chemical distribution.
Controlled annealing will reduce the degree of nanoscale lattice distortion.
Controlled annealing will homogenize the microstructure.
Local magnetoelastic coupling amplified by lattice distortion increases magnetic entropy change under low applied fields.
The disordered matrix supports fast heat exchange.
The disordered matrix supports mechanical stability.
Annealing-induced reduction of lattice distortion will diminish the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-cast state.
Annealing may increase magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-cast state.
Annealing may slow heat transfer relative to the as-cast state.
The as-cast baseline possesses pronounced nanoscale lattice distortions.
The as-cast baseline has a strong magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
The proposed relationship is limited to chemically disordered, rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys at fields below 1 T and particularly near the Curie temperature.

contradictions.description: Changes in hysteresis and heat exchange are described as merely potential and composition-dependent, yet the falsification rule says that failure to observe either type of change independently falsifies the hypothesis. That rule is stronger than the qualified predictions.
